An unnamed restricted board already came back Big before the fix. (5) OWNER: I agree. Under CONTRACTS 4, 'Board as its BoardSpec (rebuilt with resolveBoard)', with BoardSpec = string | { cartan; xy? }, no spec rebuilds F4 with labels [4,3,2,1]: a name gives the standard board (SPEC 6.6), and a matrix gives Big with labels 1..n. Carrying labels and name needs a new wire field and a board copy, built in the site, whose name is not the standard board of that name. One precedent: P1-A2 already added arith: 'Big' to the wire as a plan addition (DECISIONS.md:455), so the owner could rule option (a) a plan-level addition instead of a contract rewrite. Choosing between (a), (b) and (c) is still a format decision that RT-FIX 7.2 leaves to the owner. The empty board cannot cross within the contract: resolveBoard 'throws on not-a-board' (CONTRACTS 4), and the engine exports no 0-node constructor (CONTRACTS 2). The prompt rejection keeps the class (NotABoard), and no reader reaches it, because t13/load.ts:58 and :68 (noWhiteNode) make no call for that case.

needs-decision. This is a duplicate of P6-RT-03-02, with the same cause (specOf) and the same remaining part. Original reproducer redteam-RT-06-p6-worker-satake.test.ts, untracked, in the same run as above: '2 failed | 16 passed (18)'. The failing tests are 'E8 e8(-24): satake, restrictedBoard and matchCatalogue equal the direct call' and 'E8 e8(-24): the restricted board that comes back from the worker is the board the main thread computes (matrix, labels)'. Each diff now shows only three things: bigint entries (2n against 2, and the arith object's one and zero as 1n and 0n), labels [1,2,3,4] against [4,3,2,1], and the missing name 'F4'. The matrix in position order is the main thread's [[2,-1,0,0],[-1,2,-2,0],[0,-1,2,-1],[0,0,-1,2]]; at the gate the -2 and -1 were swapped. satake and matchCatalogue round-trip exactly for all 8 E7 and E8 records, and the island tests pass. So the behaviour the finding describes, the board coming back as the canonical F4 with another matrix, is gone; only the label, name and SafeInt loss of BoardSpec remains. The comment '// regression: P6-RT-06-02' is at workerWire-named-board.test.ts:117 and :134. Scratch revert B (workerWire.ts set to 7faf7b9) made all 3 tests of that file fail, as quoted for P6-RT-03-02, and I restored the file. Arithmetic: only rb.board of e8(-24) is affected, and T13 never reads it (see P6-RT-03-02). I agree it needs the owner, for the same reason: BoardSpec has no labels, and a name gives the standard board. The lens's alternative, reordering or naming boards in the engine, changes the engine's output and the E-7 plan reading of P4-A1 and P6-A1, which is not open to a fixer.
